# Hook Generator for TikTok: 50 Ready-to-Film Hooks for 5 Creator Niches

If you searched for "hook generator for tiktok," you probably don't want a lecture on hooks. You want lines you can say out loud in the first three seconds of your next video. This page gives you 50 of them, grouped by creator niche. Each hook has three parts:

- **Spoken line:** what you say on camera, kept to about 12 words so it fits in three seconds.
- **On-screen text:** the overlay viewers read with the sound off.
- **Hook type:** one of five types (curiosity, contrarian, stakes, result, callout), so you can A/B test types against each other instead of guessing.

Every example was written with the Hook Lab method: a positioning angle first, then hooks specific to the topic, with types mixed for testing. Where a hook needs a real number from you, it shows `[ADD: your number]`. Put your own verified figure there. Never make one up.

---

## How to Choose and Test Your TikTok Hooks

**Choose**
- **Match the hook to the payoff.** The first three seconds make a promise, and the rest of the video has to keep it. A curiosity hook with no reveal teaches viewers to scroll past you next time.
- **Say it out loud and time it.** If it runs past about three seconds, cut words. Most hooks lose filler like "so," "hey guys," or "today I want to."
- **Write on-screen text that works on mute.** Many people watch with the sound off. Your overlay should create the same pull as the spoken line, without copying it word for word.
- **Use only real numbers.** A result hook is strongest when the number is yours and true. If you don't have one yet, use a curiosity or contrarian hook.

**Test**
1. Pick one video idea and write three hooks for it, each a different type (for example, contrarian, callout, and result).
2. Film the body of the video once. Re-record only the first three seconds for each hook.
3. Post the versions on separate days at a similar time, so the hook is the only thing that changes.
4. Compare the analytics TikTok gives you in its native dashboard, especially retention in the first few seconds and average watch time. Write down which hook type won.
5. After a few rounds, look at which types win most often for your audience. Lean on those, but keep testing one new type now and then.

## FAQ

**What is a hook generator for TikTok?**
It's a tool or method that writes the opening line of a short video, meaning the first three seconds that decide whether someone keeps watching. A good one gives you several options of different types, each with a spoken line and on-screen text, so you can test them instead of guessing.

**How long should a TikTok hook be?**
Aim for about 12 spoken words or fewer, so it fits in roughly three seconds. On-screen text should be shorter still, something a viewer can read at a glance.

**Should the spoken hook and on-screen text say the same thing?**
Not exactly. They should support each other. The overlay often works best as a short, punchy version or a complementary angle, so people watching on mute still get pulled in.

**Can I use these hooks on Reels and YouTube Shorts too?**
Yes. The first-three-seconds rule applies on all three short-form platforms. Adjust the length of the full script to each platform, and check that your on-screen text sits clear of each app's interface buttons.
